input: This summary reviews delivery performance at a contract packaging firm which runs 2 plants and has revenue of $74 million per year, drawing on order records for 12 months covering 14591 orders. On-time delivery over the last two quarters was 84%, against a target of 95%, and the shortfall is concentrated rather than evenly spread, since Plant 2 accounts for 61% of late orders. Overtime cost was $2.1 million last year, up 27% on the year before, and the order backlog stands at 4.2 weeks, against 2.1 weeks a year ago, which suggests that the lateness problem is being carried forward rather than cleared. A scheduling system for all plants is quoted at $320k, whereas Plant 2 alone is $133k, and an internal estimate (not a vendor figure) puts the overtime reduction at Plant 2 at 15-20% in the first year. The recommendation under consideration is to install at Plant 2 first and hold the other plants until Plant 2 results are reported, with the operations director owning the scheduling programme. The concentration of the lateness in a single plant is, on the face of the records, the strongest argument for the staged course, since it allows the effect of the system to be observed where the problem is most acute before a decision is taken about the remaining plant.
